subject.title: fix: reconcile timed-out gateway message actions

question: Should Gateway message-action timeout reconciliation prevent duplicate delivery only while the current Gateway process survives, or must it also survive a Gateway restart?
rationale: Current main supports same-key joining and five-minute result caching within one Gateway process, while restart-safe behavior would require a materially different persisted operation or receipt contract.

options.title: Accept process-lifetime reconciliation
options.body: Merge after seam-level and live proof, with Gateway restart during the ambiguous window explicitly outside the guaranteed behavior.

options.title: Require restart-safe delivery
options.body: Hold the PR until message-action operation state or delivery receipts survive Gateway restart.

options.title: Defer transport reconciliation
options.body: Pause this PR and rely on higher-level duplicate controls while a broader delivery-outcome contract is designed.

recommendation.title: Accept process-lifetime reconciliation
recommendation.body: Merge after seam-level and live proof, with Gateway restart during the ambiguous window explicitly outside the guaranteed behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: He most recently owned the shared outbound Gateway timeout policy and has broad history across the affected delivery boundary.
